title: SPA/318/2021 of SANJAY KUMAR BHATT Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
THE HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE SRI RAGHVENDRA SINGH CHAUHAN
AND
THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE ALOK KUMAR VERMA
SPECIAL APPEAL No. 318 OF 2021
27TH SEPTEMBER, 2021
Between:
Sanjay Kumar Bhatt. ...Appellant.
and
State of Uttarakhand and others. Respondents.
Counsel for the appellant.

: Mr. Navnish Negi, the learned counsel.
Counsel for the respondents.

: Mr. K.N. Joshi, the learned Deputy
Advocate General for the State of
Uttarakhand.
The Court made the following:
JUDGMENT : (per Hon'ble The Chief Justice Sri Raghvendra Singh Chauhan)
 Aggrieved by the order dated 18.08.2021,
passed by the learned Single Judge, in Writ Petition
(M/S) No. 1534 of 2021, the appellant has preferred the
present Special Appeal. By the said order, the learned
Single Judge had dismissed the Writ Petition filed by the
appellant-writ petitioner, wherein the appellant-writ
petitioner had sought a mandamus commanding the
respondent no. 3 to assess the damages caused to the
property of the petitioner, and to consider the

2
compensation of the damaged property in accordance
with law.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall
be referred to as arrayed in the Writ Petition.
3. According to the petitioner, he is the owner of
Hotel Holy Sangam situated at National Highway No.58,
Near Devprayag Bus Stand, Tehri Garhwal. The said
property also includes a Banquet Hall, which is just
above the National Highway No.58. Under the All
Weather Roads Project, the said National Highway had
to be widened. Accordingly, the Public Works
Department, Srinagar, Garhwal undertook the process of
cutting of the road. The widening and cutting of the
road adjacent to the Hotel of the petitioner, in the
month of March/April, 2020, led to heavy land sliding in
the area, which resulted in damage to the petitioner's
Banquet Hall.
4. The petitioner made a complaint to the
Executive Engineer, National Highway (NH No.58),
Srinagar Garhwal that due to heavy rainfall and land

3
sliding, a part of his Hotel has been washed away. And
the Banquet Hall has been damaged due to the non-construction of the retaining wall and the negligent road
cutting work undertaken by the Department. In
response to the aforesaid complaint of the petitioner, the
Office of the respondent no. 3, in its report dated
01.09.2020, sent to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Tehri
Garhwal, admitted the fact that there has been partial
damage to the property of the petitioner. According to
the respondent No.3, the repair work and the
construction of the retaining wall could not be done due
to the lockdown in the State. On 18.01.2021, the
petitioner again submitted a representation to the
authorities. By its letter dated 18.02.2021, the office of
respondent no. 3, wrote to the petitioner that the
damage caused to the property of the petitioner would
be repaired within a week. On 05.03.2021, the
petitioner again represented before the office of the
Executive Engineer, National Highway No.58, that the
repair works have not been started as yet. In reply to
the said representation, on 06.03.2021, the office of the
respondent no. 3 directed the agency undertaking the
contract work to expedite the work of repair, and to

4
reconstruct the retaining wall in the damaged area.
Finally, on 01.04.2021, the office of the respondent no.
3 issued a letter seeking survey of the damaged
property of the petitioner and to assess the same by the
Special Land Acquisition Officer/ADM, Tehri Garhwal so
that the matter could be disposed of accordingly.
5. On 05.06.2021, the petitioner again made a
representation to the Executive Engineer, NH No.58,
Srinagar Garhwal, wherein he stated that despite
repeated assurances, the reconstruction and repair work
has not been undertaken for almost a period of one
year. In order to save his property from further damage
from the upcoming monsoon season, the petitioner has
done partial repair work to raise the retaining wall at the
damaged site. Hence, the department should pay the
appropriate compensation to the petitioner.
6. Thereafter, a survey of the damaged site was
undertaken by the Department in the presence of the
petitioner for proper assessment of the damage caused
to the property.

5
7. Since the petitioner was aggrieved by the
inaction of the respondent-authorities, the petitioner
filed a Writ Petition before a learned Single Judge of this
Court. However, by order dated 18.08.2021, the
learned Single Judge has dismissed the Writ Petition,
with a liberty to the petitioner to avail any other
appropriate legal remedy available to him under the law.
Hence, the present Special Appeal before this Court.
8. At the outset, Mr. Navnish Negi, the learned
counsel for the petitioner, frankly concedes that the
petitioner is not entitled to claim any damages under
Section 12 of the Right to Fair Compensation and
Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and
Resettlement Act, 2013. However, relying on the case of
Kawaljeet Singh Talwar vs. State of Uttarakhand &
others, [2018 (1) U.D. 17], the learned counsel
pleads that since the amount to be paid by the
respondents to the petitioner in an undisputed amount,
which is beyond the pale of doubt, the Writ Court can
certainly entertain a writ petition. Therefore, the learned
Single Judge was unjustified in concluding that a writ of
mandamus could not be issued to the respondents.

6
9. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant.
10. The position being taken by the learned
counsel is clearly untenable. For, the case of Kawaljeet
Singh Talwar (supra) dealt with the breach of contract.
However, the present case is not a case of breach of
contract. Moreover, since the petitioner claims that his
property has been damaged, since the petitioner is
claiming damages from the respondents, obviously, the
quantum of damages to be paid to the petitioner is un-quantified so far. What is the reasonable damage to be
paid by the respondents to the petitioner is a question of
fact. Such disputed question of fact cannot be gone into
by the Writ Court. Therefore, the learned Single Judge
was justified in concluding that a writ of mandamus
cannot be issued to the respondents.
11. Moreover, in order to be fair to the petitioner,
the learned Single Judge has granted the liberty to the
petitioner to avail other appropriate remedies which are
open to him. Therefore, this Court does not find any

7
illegality or perversity in the impugned order dated
18.08.2021, passed by the learned Single Judge.
12. This appeal being devoid of any merit is,
hereby, dismissed.
13. No order as to costs.
 _____________________________
RAGHVENDRA SINGH CHAUHAN, C.J.
___________________
ALOK KUMAR VERMA, J.
Dt: 27th September, 2021
NISHANT
